description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

Zable is about to become the face of Lendable. We’re rebranding the company and product, significantly increasing our D2C marketing investment, and building out a marketing function under our newly appointed CMO. It’s one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, backed by real financial strength, a large customer base and a product people love.

Partnerships and sponsorships will be central to how we grow, and we’re building the team to make that happen. As our Growth Partnerships Manager, you’ll shape the strategy and the budget, not just manage the day-to-day. Reporting to the Head of Growth Partnerships, you’ll define our commercial approach, decide where partnership spend goes, and take every deal from first conversation to live activation: agreeing terms, making sure campaigns land well, and keeping partners engaged. You’ll also make the case for each investment, with the data to back it, to senior leadership.

This is a senior seat for someone who enjoys both the creative and the analytical sides of partnerships. You’ll have real budget responsibility, model payback economics, and bring colleagues with you on the big calls. If you think about CPA, rev share and LTV:CAC as naturally as you think about relationships, you’ll feel at home here.

What we're looking for:

Essential:

  • 5+ years in partnerships, affiliate marketing, sponsorships, BD or growth roles for a consumer brand, including time spent shaping commercial strategy, not just executing it

  • Fluent in core acquisition performance metrics, CPA, Revenue share, LTV, ROI and blended CAC, and comfortable moving between them when structuring a deal

  • Working knowledge of channel economics: payback period, cohort behaviour, and how partnership spend compares against other acquisition channels

  • Direct experience running affiliate and/or influencer partnership end to end, including commercial negotiation (not just relationship management)

  • Track record of running activations end-to-end and delivering measurable results

  • Strong account / relationship management skills

  • Comfortable with the data, channel economics, attribution and ROI

  • Highly organised and detail-oriented, you can run multiple activations in parallel

  • Strong commercial communicator, you can hold your own with senior partners and senior internal stakeholders alike

  • Experience setting and owning a partnerships budget or channel P&L, with the judgement to reprioritise spend as performance data comes in

  • Comfortable presenting strategy and performance to senior leadership, and defending investment decisions with data

  • Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow

Desirable:

  • Experience in fintech or financial services

  • Experience with sport, entertainment, media or large brand sponsorships

  • Experience with an affiliate network or tracking platform (e.g. Impact, Awin, CJ, Partnerize) and reading platform-level reporting unassisted

  • Experience with affiliate, influencer or embedded finance partnerships

  • Some deal structuring experience

  • Experience line-managing or mentoring a more junior partnerships or affiliate executive

You’re a good fit if you’re:

  • A natural relationship-builder, partners trust you, and so does your team

  • A strategic thinker as much as a doer, you can zoom out to set the plan, then zoom back in to execute it yourself

  • Commercially literate first, relationship-led second, you measure success in growth, not vanity

  • A strong project manager, you keep things moving and on-budget

  • Data-fluent , you build your own view on what’s working from raw performance data, not just a dashboard summary

  • Hands-on and resourceful, you make things happen

  • Curious about AI and how it changes the partnerships discipline

What you'll be doing

Leadership & Strategy:

  • Set the partnerships strategy and roadmap, and own the case for investment with senior leadership

  • Mentor and support a more junior partnerships or affiliate executive

  • Represent the partnerships function in senior leadership and budget reviews

Commercial & Performance:

  • Negotiate commercial terms with affiliates, influencers and sponsorship partners – CPA, Revenue share, hybrid and flat-fee structures – and know which model fit the partner

  • Own the partnerships budget and unit economics of every live partnership: track CAC by channel and partner against LTV, and flag anything trending the wrong way before it becomes a budget problem

  • Build and maintain the channel-economics view that lets the team compare partnership spend against other acquisition channels

  • Manage affiliate network/platform relationships (tracking, reconciliation, payout accuracy) and be the first port of call when number don’t match

Activation:

  • Run sponsorship and partnership activations end-to-end, brief, plan, ship, measure

  • Manage the day-to-day with partners: planning, comms, escalations

  • Coordinate across creative, growth, lifecycle and legal

Partner Management:

  • Own the partner relationship, be the trusted operator they call first

  • Manage budgets and timelines across activations

  • Spot opportunities to expand existing partnerships based on their performance data

Performance & Optimisation:

  • Track partnership performance against targets, CPA, CAC, LTV, ROI, Rev Share payout

  • Build the playbooks and tooling that scale the function, including standard commercial terms by partner type

  • Use AI to scale research, brief-writing and reporting

Cross-functional:

  • Partner with creative on activation assets

  • Partner with finance and legal on contracts and accruals and commission reconciliation

  • Report on partnership performance to the Head of Growth Partnerships, with the numbers to back every recommendation

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

Our mobile app, Zable, is how most of our customers experience all of our products in one centralised space. It's written in React Native and TypeScript with a Kotlin backend, shipped to iOS and Android from a single codebase. We are now looking to level up the quality engineering so that we can raise release cadence without losing sleep over regressions.

This is an automation-first role. You'll spend most of your time writing code - test frameworks, CI tooling, helpers, rather than executing test scripts by hand. You'll work alongside software engineers, product, and design, setting direction.

You'll also be working at the frontier of AI-assisted quality, using LLMs and AI tooling to speed up test authoring, triage failures, and surface coverage gaps, while applying the engineering judgement to keep tests trustworthy.

What you'll be doing

Own the mobile test strategy:

  • Define and evolve a pragmatic test pyramid for React Native - deciding where E2E is worth the weight and where logic belongs in faster layers (Jest, React Testing Library, component tests).

  • Make deliberate calls about coverage, reliability, and speed trade-offs across the app.

  • Set the bar for what "ready to ship" looks like on mobile, and hold the line on it.

Build reliable E2E automation:

  • Create and maintain mobile E2E suites in Maestro, including the scaffolding around them - test data, device configuration, helpers, reporting.

  • Integrate suites into CI (GitHub Actions) so engineers get fast, trustworthy feedback on every PR and release candidates carry a signal people actually believe.

  • Drive flakiness down and time-to-diagnosis down. We treat a flaky test the same way we treat a broken test, and we expect root-cause work rather than retry-until-green.

Bring AI into the SDLC:

  • Use AI tools day-to-day to accelerate test authoring, cluster failures, surface coverage insights, and propose fixes.

description:

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

The Internal Communications Lead will build the machine and communications culture that keep Faculty's leadership and teams genuinely connected as we scale - carrying vision, strategy and our worldview on AI to every team undiluted, and surfacing the stories from across the business worth telling

This role has two core mandates:

1. Building the internal communications machine - you will design and own how leadership and our teams stay connected day to day - whether live or written, scheduled or ad hoc, and whatever formats a genuinely global, always-on business needs. You will build the architecture - cadence, ownership, structure - so the right message reaches the right people at the right moment, and noise becomes context rather than clutter.

2. Culture, Voice & Connection at Scale - you will be the person who makes sure leadership's vision, strategy and worldview on AI actually reach our teams everywhere, honest and crisp, without being diluted, delayed, or lost in translation as we grow. Leadership owns their voice and their point of view - that stays theirs. Your job is building the stage it's delivered from: sharp, timely, and sensitive to how a message lands differently across cultures and geographies.

What you own

  • The voice going down - The communications framework and rhythm that allow the Faculty Leadership to effectively communicate their vision, strategy and worldview on AI to every team, wherever they are in the world, undiluted and on time.

  • The voice from Accenture to Faculty - Point person for relevant Accenture news, updates and requirements that the Faculty teams need to know.

  • The detective work - Some of the best things happening at Faculty aren’t visible from the top. A team quietly solved a hard client problem. Someone's work never got the credit it deserved. A pattern of small wins nobody's connected into a story yet. You go looking for this, building the instincts and the relationships across the business to find the stories worth telling.

  • How we organise ourselves to communicate effectively - The architecture and judgment behind all of it so our people get a clear read of what matters without being buried under what doesn't.

What you will be doing

Forums & Formats

  • Design the company-wide forums that carry leadership's message, choosing the right format for the right moment rather than defaulting to habit

  • Build for global and cultural nuance from the start, so a message crafted in one office lands with the same weight and clarity in every other

  • Establish a working cadence that respects people's time and attention, so more communication is never mistaken for better communication

Channel Architecture & Cadence

  • Own the internal channel architecture, so messages reach the right people without adding to the volume everyone already wades through

  • Set clear ownership of who can broadcast to the whole company, on what, and how often

  • Bring judgement to every leadership message: which forum, format, tone and timing will make it land, and the confidence to say when something needs live delivery, a short note, or nothing broad at all

Storytelling & Culture

  • Play detective for the stories that don't naturally surface and give them the visibility they deserve

  • Treat culture preservation as a first-order responsibility of scale, not a side effect of good comms: building formats that carry how Faculty's leaders and teams work together, not just what the business is doing

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Where needed, partner closely with leadership as a trusted advisor, protecting their voice while making sure it travels well

  • Establish strong cross-functional relationships across regions and teams to understand what's really happening in the business and shape the internal communications programme around it

  • Support the international expansion of Faculty's internal communications, working with regional colleagues to ensure forums and formats travel well and adapt where they need to

What we are looking for

  • Designing the Machine - A track record of designing and building the machine from scratch - cadences, channels, and company-wide forums - rather than simply running an existing playbook.

  • Judgement - A sharp instinct for signal versus noise: what deserves broad visibility, what doesn't, and the confidence to say so to senior stakeholders.

  • Storytelling - A detective's instinct for finding the story in a large, fast-moving organisation, and the ability to tell it with clarity and a genuine point of view.

  • Global & Cultural Fluency - Proven experience communicating across geographies and time zones, with real sensitivity to how messages land differently across cultures and offices.

  • Stakeholder Management - Skilled at working alongside senior leaders and founders, earning trust quickly through sound judgement and discretion.

  • Communication - Exceptional written and verbal skills, able to convey a complex or nuanced leadership message clearly and briefly without losing what made it worth saying.

  • Change & Scale Experience - Experience communicating through a period of fast growth, acquisition, or significant organisational change, ideally in a technical or fast-moving industry.

  • Autonomy & Resilience - Highly self-sufficient, with the flexibility and tenacity to thrive in a fast-paced, complex scale-up environment now operating at global scale.

Our Interview Process

  1. Talent Team Screen (30mins)

  2. Introduction with the Hiring Manager (60 mins)

  3. Panel Interview involving pre work (75 mins)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

About the job

Are you someone with a passion for DevOps and are looking to help build and be part of a new Developer Experience team within the Motorway Product & Engineering org? Motorway continues to grow, and we want to provide our developers with the best experience, which is where you come in.

We have recently built and rolled out a new container platform on top of AWS Fargate, and are currently enhancing our observability, reliability, and developer-focused tooling. We will continue to build and evolve secure, standardised platform capabilities that reduce cognitive load and help teams ship faster with confidence.

This is an exciting time to join, the team is new and the company growing which presents opportunities to do things “right” to set up success for the org into the future.

What you'll do

  • Own and evolve our AWS environments and shared platform infrastructure, focusing on reliability, scalability, and ease of use for product teams.

  • Design and build opinionated, self-service tooling that makes it easy for engineers to build, deploy, and operate services correctly.

  • Continuously reduce manual work (toil) by automating common workflows and standardising infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code and platform abstractions.

  • Define and implement platform-level monitoring and alerting standards that provide meaningful signals without overwhelming teams.

  • Enable product teams to use shared metrics and signals to understand and improve the reliability of their services across environments.

  • Own and evolve our continuous delivery and release capabilities, reducing time to production while maintaining high standards of reliability and safety.

  • Stay current with best practices in application hosting, continuous delivery, and developer experience, and apply them pragmatically to the platform.

  • Upskill and mentor other engineers in the team.

As a senior engineer, you are expected to bring prior experience operating and evolving production platforms at scale. You’ll use your judgement to make trade-offs, anticipate failure modes, and help the team avoid repeating past mistakes. Learning is encouraged and supported, but you should be comfortable operating independently after onboarding and sharing lessons from real-world experience.

Requirements

  • Proven track record of owning and operating web platforms in production at scale.

  • Strong experience with AWS in a production environment.

  • Experience defining meaningful metrics, monitoring, and alerting for web platforms, with a strong intuition for actionable vs noisy signals.

  • Experience working with platform-level security controls and observability, including identifying and responding to abnormal or unsafe system behaviour.

  • Experience designing and operating continuous delivery systems that support safe, repeatable, zero-downtime deployments.

  • Experience responding to production incidents in an on-call environment and improving systems based on what you learn.

  • Comfortable with command-line tools and environments.

  • Proficient with at least one programming language used for automation or tooling.

  • Enjoy solving complex, cross-cutting problems in collaboration with engineers across the organisation

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and priorities.

  • Enjoy mentoring and sharing knowledge within the team and the wider engineering organisation.

This role includes a shared, out-of-hours on-call rotation after an initial onboarding period. On-call is supported by the wider engineering team and is designed to be sustainable and continuously improved

Benefits

  • A competitive salary

  • BUPA health insurance

  • Discounted gym membership through BUPA

  • OnHand volunteering membership and one paid volunteering day per year

  • Hybrid working

  • Pension scheme

  • Motorway car leasing scheme - lease a zero-emissions electric vehicle at a significant discount

  • Enhanced parental leave - We offer enhanced maternity pay (26 weeks of full pay) and enhanced paternity pay (4 weeks of full pay) to eligible employees.

  • Workplace nursery scheme

  • Regular social events

  • Cycle to work scheme

Equal opportunities statement

We are committed to equality of opportunity for all employees. We work to provide a supportive and inclusive environment where people can maximise their full potential. We believe our workforce should reflect a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives and experiences. Our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion is evident through our constant focus on recruiting, developing and advancing individuals based on their skills and talents.

We welcome applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

We will continue to build and evolve secure, standardised platform capabilities that reduce cognitive load and help teams ship faster with confidence.

As a Developer Experience Security Engineer, you will ensure that security is built into how engineers build, deploy, and operate software, making the secure path the easiest path you will ensure that security is built into how engineers build, deploy, and operate software.

This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role. You'll also work closely with - and may grow into ownership of - adjacent parts of our Alternative Offers and in-store rewards portfolio.

title: AI Research Engineer (London)
description:
About Edra

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.


The Role

We're building a learning system that teaches AI agents how enterprises actually work. Our system starts from what a customer already has: knowledge base articles, support conversations, tickets, system logs, and agent traces. From that evidence it reverse-engineers how the business actually runs and writes the process down as instructions a person can inspect and an agent can execute, with confidence scoring to know when to automate and when to seek human input.

We're looking for AI Research Engineers who have built complex, production LLM-based systems. Whether you've scaled LLM workflows handling millions of requests, built multi-agent systems in production, or designed evaluation frameworks for enterprise deployments, we want people who bring intensity and self-direction to their craft. You'll work on our agentic learning environment: the loops that turn human corrections and agent outcomes into better knowledge and instructions over time. The job combines applied research with ownership of production systems. You find a failure, form a hypothesis, run the experiment, and ship the fix into real customer workflows.

You'll spend most of your time advancing our core context-learning library and the harness that powers our agents across every customer. The work spans continuous learning, context engineering, agent orchestration, and evaluation. You'll contribute to our knowledge benchmarks and to the self-improving capabilities of the harness.


What You'll Do

  • Build and extend our core context-learning library, turning customer-informed problems into reusable platform capabilities.

  • Design and implement LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows from concept to production.

  • Build agentic features for knowledge management: agents that can edit, update, and maintain large knowledge bases autonomously.

  • Build continuous learning loops that use human corrections and production outcomes to find knowledge gaps, detect changed procedures, and improve prompts and instructions.

  • Build reliability and confidence systems: evaluation frameworks, confidence scoring, and logic for when to automate and when to escalate to a human.

  • Architect async, scalable systems that handle complex AI orchestration.

  • Contribute to the direction of our AI strategy and product capabilities.


What We’re Looking For

title: AIT Systems Integration Engineer
description:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.

You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.

The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.

Responsibilities

Functional and system testing

  • Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.

  • Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.

  • Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.

  • Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.

  • Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.

  • Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.

Verification tracking

  • Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.

  • Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.

  • Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.

  • Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.

GSE and test infrastructure

  • Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.

  • Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.

  • Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.

Integration and campaign support

  • Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.

  • Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.

  • Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.

  • Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.

Requirements

  • Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.

  • Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.

  • Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.

  • Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.

  • Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.

  • Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.

  • Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.

  • Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.

  • Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).

  • Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.

Desirables

  • End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.

  • Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).

  • Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).

  • Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.

  • Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).

  • Launch campaign experience at a launch site.

  • Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.

  • Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.

Personal attributes

  • Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.

  • Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.

  • Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.

  • Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.

  • Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

  • Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

  • Insights & Analytics: Own the analysis of social performance, customer behaviour and competitor activity. Turn data into clear insights and recommendations, using performance to continuously improve our strategy.

  • Key collaboration: Partner with the Head of Performance Marketing to create a boosting strategy
  • Social Innovation: Keep TALA ahead of how social is evolving, from new platforms and formats to creators, communities and emerging behaviours, ensuring we continue to find new ways to grow our audience.

Requirements

Atolls is the world's largest community-driven shopping platform, active in 20+ markets. 

We help millions make smarter spending decisions across discovery, evaluation, and (re-)purchase by connecting people with the right brands and retailers.

About This Role:

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to take ownership of our Gift Cards vertical - one of the fastest-growing parts of our alternative offers, spanning gift card purchase, redemption, provider partnerships, and cross-market growth across UK, Germany, and Spain.

You'll set the strategy for a business line generating triple-digit YoY growth in some markets, own the commercial relationships with our gift card providers, and work directly with our Fulfilment leadership on where the vertical goes next. You'll also work closely with - and may grow into ownership of - adjacent parts of our Alternative Offers and in-store rewards portfolio.

We want a strong senior product leader: someone who has built and scaled products at a leading tech company and/or a startup, who thinks and acts like an entrepreneur, and who can move a commercial product forward with minimal hand-holding.

At Atolls, we believe in nurturing both your professional and personal growth. Here's what you can expect:

  • A culture that values personal and professional development, with internal mobility opportunities.
  • A supportive and open-minded team that embraces diverse perspectives and innovative ideas.
  • 32 days of paid vacation plus your birthday off, giving you the time you need to recharge.
  • A flexible hybrid working scheme to balance work and life.
  • Access to a learning budget and internal training to help you grow in your role.
  • Mental health coaching to support your well-being.
  • Regular global and local get-togethers to celebrate successes and build connections.
  • The possibility of taking a sabbatical after three years with the company.

*These are global benefits that apply to all employees, with additional local perks based on your location.

Responsibilities:

In this role, you will:

  • Own the gift card product strategy and roadmap - from provider selection and inventory quality to the end-to-end purchase, redemption, and admin experience.
  • Lead commercial and provider negotiations - framework agreements, commission structures, SLAs, and multi-entity contracting with gift card providers (e.g. Finperks, Tillo), in partnership with Operations, Legal and Finance.
  • Drive revenue growth across markets - set and deliver GMV and commission targets across France, Germany, and Spain, backed by rigorous transaction-level analysis.
  • Partner cross-functionally - work daily with engineering, design, data, CRM, and adjacent product teams to ship a coherent gift card experience across web, app, and browser extension.
  • Use data to lead, not just report - build and refine models (e.g. fraud-tier scoring), validate revenue and performance data with Finance, and identify the next highest-impact bet.
  • Represent the vertical at the leadership level - bring clear recommendations and trade-offs to cross-team and leadership forums, and help shape Alternative Offers' broader strategic direction.
  • Build for scale - help expand gift cards from a standalone catalogue page into a fully integrated offer type across the platform.

 Your Profile:

  • 5+ years in product management, including significant time owning a product or business line end-to-end at a leading tech company and/or a startup.
  • A strong entrepreneurial track record - you've built something from close to zero, made judgment calls with imperfect data, and taken ownership beyond your formal remit.
  • Commercial fluency - comfortable owning revenue targets, running vendor/partner negotiations, and thinking in margin, commission, and unit economics, not just features.
  • Strong analytical skills - fluent working with transaction and revenue data to make and defend decisions; comfortable partnering with data/finance teams on models like fraud scoring.
  • Proven cross-functional leadership - experience leading engineering, design, and data counterparts in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, without formal authority over them.
  • Excellent stakeholder management - able to influence and present confidently to senior/executive stakeholders.
  • A degree from a top-tier university (e.g. Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, HEC Paris, ESSEC, Sciences Po, Bocconi, ETH Zurich, or equivalent); an MBA or further qualification from a leading program is a plus.
  • Fluent English required

As the AI technical lead for your domain, you will drive architecture decisions, engineering excellence, and AI adoption across teams and stakeholders. Examples of domains include: Sales, GTM and Marketing or Finance & Legal

Generative AI and AI Agents are fundamentally reshaping commerce software and the way our teams work on a day to day basis.

At Mirakl, AI is becoming a core part of our product strategy. From Catalog Transformer and content generation to AI Agents and Agentic Commerce, we are building the next generation of commerce software. And we have the same ambition for our teams around AI products and adoption.

We are looking for a Lead AI Engineer to transform cutting-edge AI technologies into reliable, scalable, and measurable products used by leading enterprises worldwide.

title: Mid Market Sales Manager (Paris)
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

We’re hiring a Sales Leader to build Dust’s go-to-market presence across French Mid-Market and SMB customers. This is an opportunity to shape how we reach and grow a broad range of businesses, from developing an efficient sales motion to helping customers see value quickly and expand over time.

You’ll act as the business lead for the segment, with accountability for revenue. You’ll lead and coach the sales team, stay close to customers and deals, and build a repeatable approach that balances efficient execution with the different needs of SMB and Mid-Market customers.

You’ll also coordinate the teams that support pipeline generation, sales, and customer growth. Working closely with BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, you’ll focus resources on the channels and activities that can best support the segment’s goals.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow the sales team for the Mid-Market and SMB segment, including hiring, performance, and day-to-day execution.

  • Own the segment’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Set priorities with the CRO, review progress, and address gaps early.

  • Define and refine the sales approach for SMB and Mid-Market customers, adapting qualification, messaging, and deal support to each customer’s needs.

  • Build an efficient path from target account and first conversation through qualification, evaluation, close, handoff, and expansion.

  • Coach sellers on discovery, value-based selling, pipeline discipline, and helping customers make decisions with confidence.

  • Make clear, evidence-based recommendations to Product based on customer conversations, deal patterns, and segment needs.

  • Work with BDR and Growth leaders to build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound and other relevant channels.

  • Partner with Field Marketing to prioritize campaigns, events, customer advocacy, and community programs that support pipeline and revenue goals. Work within the marketing leadership’s standards and methods, and ensure programs are well executed and measured.

  • Set direction for how Partnerships can support segment priorities, working with the Partnerships lead on relevant sourcing, co-selling, and delivery opportunities.

  • Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to support effective evaluations, smooth implementations, adoption, and expansion.

  • Share market learning with the CRO and other segment leads, helping Dust develop a coherent France go-to-market approach.

What we’re looking for

  • A proven B2B software sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help sellers succeed.

  • Experience selling to SMB and Mid-Market customers, with the judgment to adapt the sales motion to different deal sizes, buying processes, and customer needs.

  • A track record of owning a segment or market revenue number end to end and building pipeline through functions you did not directly manage.

  • Experience coaching sellers, building a reliable forecast, and creating consistent sales practices.

  • Good commercial judgment about where to focus team capacity and budget, including how direct sales, marketing, and partners can support growth.

  • Strong collaboration skills across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, RevOps, and post-sales teams.

  • High EQ, clear communication, and a supportive but accountable leadership style.

  • Comfort building repeatable sales practices in a scaling organization. French fluency and strong working English are important.

What success looks like

The Mid-Market and SMB segment has clear sales ownership, a focused pipeline, and progress against its ARR goals. Sellers are well coached and can execute an efficient, repeatable motion suited to their customers. Cross-functional support is aligned to segment priorities, and learning from customers and deals helps Dust improve how it serves and grows SMB and Mid-Market accounts in France.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

We’re hiring a Strategic Sales Leader to build Dust’s go-to-market presence with its most important French customers. This is a pivotal opportunity to shape how we win and grow strategic accounts, from developing senior relationships and navigating complex buying groups to building a repeatable approach for large, high-impact opportunities.

You’ll act as the business lead for the strategic segment, with accountability for revenue. You’ll lead and coach the sales team while staying close to customers, account plans, and active deals. You’ll build a focused pipeline and a sales motion suited to organizations with complex needs, multiple stakeholders, and ambitious transformation goals.

You’ll also orchestrate the cross-functional support needed to grow strategic accounts. Working closely with BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, you’ll direct resources toward the accounts and opportunities where they can have the greatest impact.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow the Strategic sales team, including hiring, performance management, and day-to-day execution.

  • Own the segment’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Set clear priorities with the CRO, review progress, and address gaps early.

  • Develop a focused strategy for target accounts, including account plans, senior stakeholder relationships, and a clear view of customer priorities and decision processes.

  • Lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from first conversation through qualification, evaluation, negotiation, close, handoff, and expansion.

  • Coach sellers on executive engagement, value-based selling, multi-threading, commercial strategy, and navigating complex buying groups.

  • Build a consistent, evidence-based strategic sales motion, refining qualification, messaging, and execution based on customer conversations and deal patterns.

  • Bring customer and market learning to Product, making clear recommendations on strategic customer needs, use cases, and opportunities.

  • Set pipeline priorities with BDR and Growth leaders, including targeted outbound and other channels suited to strategic accounts.

  • Partner with Field Marketing to prioritize executive events, campaigns, customer advocacy, and community programs that support strategic pipeline and revenue goals. Work within the marketing leadership’s standards and methods, and ensure programs are well executed and measured.

  • Set direction for how Partnerships can support strategic priorities, working with the Partnerships lead on account access, co-selling, and delivery opportunities.

  • Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to deliver credible evaluations, successful implementations, adoption, and expansion.

  • Share strategic account and market insights with the CRO and other segment leads, helping shape a coherent France go-to-market approach.

What we’re looking for

  • A proven B2B software sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help sellers succeed.

  • Experience leading Strategic or Enterprise sales, including complex, multi-stakeholder deals and relationships with senior executives.

  • A track record of owning a segment or market revenue number end to end, and building pipeline through teams and functions you did not directly manage.

  • Experience making practical decisions about where to focus capacity and budget, including the roles of direct sales, marketing, and partners.

  • Strong judgment in developing account strategies, coaching complex deal execution, and building a reliable forecast.

  • The ability to create a repeatable sales approach without treating every strategic customer as the same.

  • Strong collaboration skills across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, RevOps, and post-sales teams.

  • High EQ, clear communication, and a supportive but accountable leadership style.

  • Comfort building strategic sales practices in a scaling organization. French fluency and strong working English are important.

What success looks like

The Strategic segment has clear ownership, a focused pipeline, and measurable progress against its ARR goals. The team builds trusted relationships with senior customer stakeholders and executes complex sales cycles with discipline. Cross-functional resources are aligned to the accounts and opportunities that matter most, and learning from customers and deals helps Dust sharpen its strategic sales approach in France.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

title: FTTH Security Expert
description:
About P1 Security

Founded in 2011 by serial entrepreneur and security expert Philippe Langlois, P1 Security is on a mission to secure critical and sovereign mobile networks by providing services and technologies to identify, detect and recover from critical threats and vulnerabilities.

P1 Security is one of the very few companies in the world tackling telecom security through pure Mobile and Telecom Security attacks and security from 5G and Cloud-based infrastructure Security, OpenRAN, Network Slicing and RAN Sharing, Edge Computing (MEC), down to legacy 2/3/4G Diameter, SS7 SIGTRAN attacks, GTP manipulation and fuzzing.

Our offering and expertise range from Network and Telecom Core Network Security, Intrusion Detection and Vulnerability Assessment solutions, with technology backed by more than a decade of engineering research. We are a lean scale-up, engaged in emerging markets (Eastern Europe, Middle East, Asia), Europe and North America.

The P1 Security team includes experts from telecom operators and security companies as well as renowned security researchers who regularly present unique P1 Security research at leading international security conferences & GSMA working groups. P1 Labs, the R&D branch of P1 Security, shares Open Source initiatives with the telecom security community (www.github.com/P1sec/).

We are growing the team with people who want to help write it. We are looking for experienced profiles with grounded, hands-on knowledge of telecom networks — and a real appetite for FTTx technologies in particular. Curious, creative and open-minded people who want to dig deep into a genuinely sovereign topic: the security of the mobile networks our connectivity runs on.

Job Description

If your years have been spent in FTTx — access networks, PON, CPE, provisioning, field operations — and security has always been the question you kept coming back to, talk to us. The role described below does not really exist as a box to tick yet: we care far more about the person than about an exact match with a job title. Bring the part of the picture you know best, and we will build the rest together.

What you will do

  • Audits — you will plan and run scoped, authorized penetration tests of FTTH/PON infrastructure: OLTs, ONTs/ONUs, the management systems around the ODN, and customer premises equipment.

  • PON internals — you will dig into GPON, XG-PON, XGS-PON and NG-PON2: OMCI, PLOAM, and how ONTs are authenticated and provisioned.

  • CPE and gateways — you will take them apart: firmware extraction and reverse engineering, exposed debug interfaces (UART/JTAG), hardcoded credentials, update mechanisms and web/CLI management flaws.

  • Subscribers at scale — you will look at what provisions and manages them (TR-069/CWMP, TR-369/USP, ACS/OSS/BSS integrations, zero-touch provisioning) and at the subscriber-facing edge: BNG/BRAS, PPPoE/IPoE, DHCP, RADIUS/AAA, VLAN segmentation, QoS and isolation between subscribers.

  • Convergence and infrastructure — you will follow fixed–mobile convergence (5G FWA, shared core, shared OSS/BSS, unified identity and billing) and review devices and management planes (routers, switches, aggregation equipment, NMS/EMS, SNMP, NETCONF/YANG, SSH/Telnet, APIs, privileged access) against vendor and industry hardening baselines.

  • Threat modeling — you will map attack paths for real operator environments using frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, the GSMA FASG/FS.xx guidance and the MITRE FiGHT knowledge base.

  • Findings and clients — you will turn all of this into clear, prioritized reports with proof-of-concept evidence, risk ratings and actionable remediation, present them to stakeholders, and support remediation verification and retesting.

  • The team — you will contribute to our internal tooling, test methodologies, lab environments and reusable attack playbooks.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep knowledge on Fixed-line network architecture (FTTx, DSL, Coaxial)

  • MANDATORY: Experience in security audit pentests on OT and IT infrastructure

  • Experience with vendor ecosystems such as Huawei, ZTE, Nokia, Ericsson, Calix, or Adtran FTTH equipment.

  • Familiarity with telecom security standards and frameworks: 3GPP SCAS, GSMA NESAS, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF, and ITU-T/BBF specifications.

  • Experience in red teaming or adversary emulation against critical infrastructure.

  • Relevant certifications, such as:

  • OSCP / OSEP / OSWE / OSED

  • GPEN / GXPN / GRID

  • CEH (Practical), eJPT/eCPPT, or CRTO

  • Telecom-specific training (GSMA, Black Hat/DEF CON telecom or hardware trainings)

  • Published research, CVEs, conference talks, or bug bounty history in telecom or embedded devices.

If you have a passion for telecom security and want to be part of a dynamic and innovative team, we encourage you to apply and join us in shaping the future of Telecom Security!

Language requirements

  • English - fluent speaker

  • French - optional

Further details

  • 🏢 Headquarters: Fully remote company, with headquarters in Paris - FRANCE

  • 🏠 Remote policy:

  • At P1 Security, we recognize the importance of work-life balance, and that's why our remote policy is a key part of our company culture. We understand that flexibility is crucial, allowing our team members to work remotely while achieving their personal and professional goals. To keep our team connected, we schedule monthly meetups with department members and gather the entire team on-site every two months. These regular touch points ensure effective communication, collaboration, and a dynamic team spirit, reflecting the dynamic and adaptable spirit of P1 Security. We believe in the power of flexible work arrangements to bring out the best in our team, driving success in a way that suits everyone's unique lifestyle

Hiring process

  • First contact call (10-20min)

  • Direct manager call (30min)

  • Capability assessment exercice (depending on position)

  • C-level & Director call (30 min)

Specialisations

Telecommunications Security, SS7, SIGTRAN, LTE, IMS, UMTS, CDMA, GPRS, OpenStack, Kubernetes, LinuxServers / PNF, Diameter, NFV, Security, VoLTE, VoWifi, GTP, Diameter, 3G, 4G, IoT Security, NFV(i), S1AP, X2AP, Fuzzing, eUTRAN S1AP, X2AP, NgRAN, NGAP, PFCP, 5GC SBI

Contact

If you are a motivated and experienced professional who is passionate about cybersecurity and driving innovation, we would love to hear from you! Join P1 Security and be part of a fascinating mission to protect critical infrastructure and work alongside industry experts in the cybersecurity field.

title: Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer
Senior Backend Developer
description:
Payroll that runs itself. You build the part that runs it.

quinn is an app-based managed payroll and employment-administration service for households and companies who employ people directly. The customer stays the legal employer. quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, pays salaries, social insurance and taxes, and handles every filing that follows, on their behalf and automated end to end.

We don’t sell payroll software. We run payroll.

We operate in Switzerland, Germany and the UK. Last year more than CHF 200 million in salaries ran through our systems, correct to the cent. The purpose behind it is simple: fair employment, for all.

Why this role exists

Every market brings its own authorities, insurers, pension funds and tax rules. Our answer is quinn ONE: one platform for every product and market, with a shared core for what all countries have in common and a configuration layer per country on top, designed to carry twelve countries.

The backend is that core. It is a modular monolith in C#, .NET 10 and PostgreSQL, serving one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, Maestro for batch processing, and our AI agents. Development has started, and the foundations the platform will run on for years are being laid now.

This role is fully focused on quinn ONE. Our existing products are not part of it.

What you will own

  • Backend modules, end to end. Design, build, test and run modules and the APIs they expose, from requirements to production, without waiting to be handed a ticket.

  • The data. The PostgreSQL model the platform rests on: schema design, migrations, transactions, indexing, and the calculations that must be right to the cent.

  • The foundations. Audit trail, logging, versioning of our APIs and services, and the database upgrades that keep the platform current.

  • Reliability and security in production. Tests, observability, performance, and data protection by design: an API returns what is needed, not everything that is available. Root causes, not symptoms.

  • The architecture, pragmatically. Module boundaries, dependencies, the shared core and the country layers, evolved with clear trade-offs rather than fashionable patterns.

  • The engineering bar. Code review, design discussions, and mentoring the developers around you, in Zurich and in our Armenia team.

Where the frontend ends, the backend begins. Our Product Frontend Engineer owns everything on the screen: the app, Maestro’s interface, the component library. You own everything behind it: the domain model, the payroll logic, the APIs, the integrations with authorities, insurers and banks, and the data. You agree the API contract together, and Product decides what gets built.

How we work

We are AI-native, operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how a small team ships like a large one, and how one engineer can hold the standard described here.

We expect you to live in these tools and build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, test generation, migration checks, and whatever else takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that comes with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: a transaction boundary in the wrong place, a migration that works on test data and locks a table in production. In payroll, an amount is either right or wrong. You take the speed and keep the standard.

Your first year

In your first month, you set up, learn the system and the people, and merge your first changes. Within 100 days, you have delivered the platform’s audit trail, tested and documented, and fixed the first risks you spotted on arrival.

By month nine, you are the person the team turns to for the quinn backend, and a developer you mentored is delivering features on their own. By the end of the year, the major backend roadmap items are live (logging, the database upgrade, versioning for our APIs and services), and at least one standard you introduced is used beyond your own team.

Who we are looking for

  • You have shipped and run production systems in C# and modern .NET / ASP.NET Core, and you know how they behave under load.

  • You know PostgreSQL properly: schema design, transactions, locking, indexing and query optimisation. You read the execution plan before you add a cache.

  • You have designed APIs and modules with clear boundaries and manageable dependencies.

  • You treat personal and financial data with care. Security is part of how you design, not a review at the end.

  • You use AI tools every day, and you can show where they made you faster and where you caught them being wrong.

  • You own initiatives independently and raise risks before they become surprises.

  • You review constructively, mentor willingly, and write code others can take over.

  • English is your working language. German is a plus.

What makes you stand out

  • You have worked where an amount is either right or wrong: payroll, banking, insurance, accounting or tax.

  • You have built foundations others relied on for years: an audit trail, observability, API versioning, a data model.

  • You have taken a major database upgrade or migration through production without drama.

  • You can explain what you built, why you chose your approach, and what changed because of it.

The team

We are a small, fast and direct team: engineers in Zurich working closely with our Armenia team, and colleagues across Switzerland, Germany and the UK, 40 people in all. Not much process, not much hierarchy. A clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we mean: be open, own it, speak up, keep it simple, bias for action.

We are not filling a seat. If you would rather build the core than maintain the plumbing, we would like to hear from you.

The facts

  • Location: Zürich Wiedikon, hybrid with three days a week in the office; occasional travel to the UK, Germany and our Armenia team

  • Role: Senior Backend Developer, individual contributor with technical leadership

  • Reporting line: Our Lead Engineers

  • Stack: C#, .NET 10, PostgreSQL; modular monolith

  • Pensum: 100%

  • Start: As soon as possible

  • Language: English; German a plus

Das erwartet Sie

title: Business Development Manager
description:
Grosse Veränderungen beginnen mit Menschen, die mehr erreichen wollen.

Wie kommen Mitarbeitende zur Arbeit? Warum stehen Firmenautos ungenutzt herum, während Parkplätze knapp sind? Und wie wird nachhaltige Mobilität zur attraktivsten Wahl?

Bei Urban Connect machen wir aus diesen Herausforderungen konkrete Lösungen. Wir verbinden geteilte E-Bikes und Firmenautos, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel, Mobilitätsbudgets und digitales Parkplatzmanagement auf einer Plattform. Damit helfen wir Unternehmen, Kosten zu senken, Ressourcen besser zu nutzen und ihren Mitarbeitenden mehr Freiheit zu geben.

Unternehmen wie Roche, Google, SWISS und Lonza setzen bereits auf uns. Unser Anspruch geht weiter: Wir wollen die Art verändern, wie Unternehmen Mobilität organisieren. Und wir bieten das Betriebssystem, das dies möglich macht.

Um diese Vision zu verwirklichen, suchen wir eine neugierige, unternehmerisch denkende Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Energie und gutes Urteilsvermögen mitbringt und mit uns das Unternehmen und die Mobilitätsbranche voranbringen möchte.

Deine Rolle: echte Verantwortung, spürbare Wirkung

Du möchtest ein Unternehmen mitgestalten, anspruchsvolle Probleme lösen und sehen, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.

Als Business Development Manager arbeitest du eng mit unserem Sales- und Account-Management-Team sowie mit Product, Technology und Operations zusammen. Du entwickelst aus Kundenbedürfnissen, Daten und Marktkenntnissen überzeugende Mobilitätslösungen und konkrete Wachstumschancen.

Du verantwortest Projekte, bringst eigene Ideen ein und treibst ihre Umsetzung voran. Wir erwarten, dass du von Anfang an durchdachte Fragen stellst, erkennst, wo du einen Beitrag leisten kannst, und ins Handeln kommst. Dabei unterstützen dich Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die wollen, dass du erfolgreich bist.

Was du bei uns bewegst

  • Aus Daten Chancen machen: Du analysierst Nutzungs- und Marktdaten, etwa zur Auslastung von Fahrzeugen und Parkplätzen, und entwickelst daraus umsetzbare Empfehlungen für bessere betriebliche Mobilitätslösungen.

  • Eigene Projekte vorantreiben: Du verantwortest Projekte wie Produktanalysen, die Bewertung von Geschäftschancen und die Entwicklung betrieblicher Mobilitätskonzepte. Du definierst nächste Schritte, bringst die richtigen Menschen zusammen und erzielst Ergebnisse.

  • Das Produkt verstehen: Du entwickelst ein praxisnahes Verständnis unserer Plattform, der Kundeneinrichtung, Buchungen, Abrechnungen und Integrationen. So gestaltest du Lösungen mit, die wirtschaftlich und operativ funktionieren.

  • Mit KI besser arbeiten: Du setzt KI-Tools gezielt ein, testest neue Anwendungen und verbesserst die Qualität und Effizienz unserer Recherchen, Analysen und Prozesse.

  • Wachstum vorantreiben: Du identifizierst potenzielle Kunden, verstehst ihre Herausforderungen und arbeitest mit dem Commercial-Team daran, neue Kunden zu gewinnen und bestehende Partnerschaften auszubauen.

  • Überzeugend argumentieren: Du erstellst klare Präsentationen, fundierte Business Cases, überzeugende Angebote und aussagekräftige Kundenreviews, die den Mehrwert unserer Lösungen sichtbar machen.

  • Für Fortschritt sorgen: Du setzt klare Prioritäten und hältst Kundeninformationen und nächste Schritte in HubSpot aktuell. Du hältst Zusagen ein und gehst Hindernisse frühzeitig an.

  • Teams verbinden: Du klärst technische und kommerzielle Fragen gemeinsam mit Product, Operations und Technology und leitest daraus verständliche Empfehlungen für Kunden und das Team ab.

  • Den Status quo hinterfragen: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenzial, hinterfragst Annahmen und machst aus kreativen Ideen konkrete Verbesserungen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Einen sehr guten akademischen Leistungsausweis, beispielsweise in Betriebswirtschaft, Volkswirtschaft, Data Science oder Ingenieurwissenschaften. Wissbegierde, Kreativität und nachweisbare Leistungen sind uns wichtiger als eine bestimmte Studienrichtung.

  • Relevante praktische Erfahrung im Business Development, in der Beratung, in einem Technologieunternehmen oder im unternehmerischen Umfeld. Du kannst zeigen, welche Projekte du verantwortet und welche Ergebnisse du erzielt hast.

  • Analytisches Denkvermögen, einen sicheren Umgang mit Excel und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen und Zusammenhänge zu verstehen und klar und einfach zu erklären.

  • Grosses Interesse an der Mobilität der nächsten Generation und an den Technologien, Geschäftsmodellen und Verhaltensänderungen, die die Branche prägen. Idealerweise kennst du die betriebliche Mobilitätslandschaft bereits und hast Ideen, wie sie sich verbessern lässt.

  • Gutes Urteilsvermögen: Du kannst Zielkonflikte abwägen, Wesentliches priorisieren und vorankommen, ohne auf vollständige Informationen zu warten.

  • Tatkraft und einen kreativen Zugang zur Problemlösung. Du entwickelst Vorschläge, überprüfst Annahmen und findest Wege, Dinge voranzubringen.

  • Technologieaffinität und praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Tools wie ChatGPT, Claude oder Copilot sowie das Urteilsvermögen, deren Ergebnisse kritisch zu prüfen.

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse. Französisch ist ein grosser Vorteil.

Besonders wichtig ist uns deine Haltung.

Du bringst Begeisterung, Ehrgeiz und eine lösungsorientierte Einstellung mit. Du lernst schnell, stellst durchdachte Fragen und übernimmst Verantwortung für Ergebnisse. Du achtest auf Details und suchst laufend nach Wegen, gute Arbeit noch besser zu machen.

Du bist selbstbewusst genug, eine Idee zu hinterfragen, und offen genug, deine Meinung zu ändern. Die beste Lösung und der Erfolg des Teams sind dir wichtiger als persönliche Anerkennung. Du suchst Feedback, teilst dein Wissen und arbeitest gerne mit Menschen zusammen, die das genauso halten.

Du probierst Neues aus, gehst bewusst Risiken ein und lernst aus Fehlern. Wenn du auf ein Problem stösst, ergreifst du die Initiative und beziehst andere ein, wenn es sinnvoll ist.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

Hohe Ansprüche – und kluge, herzliche Menschen, die dich fordern und weiterbringen.
Wir arbeiten ambitioniert, geben direktes, konstruktives Feedback und unterstützen uns gegenseitig. Exzellenz zeigt sich bei uns im Alltag: in durchdachten Lösungen, sorgfältiger Umsetzung und dem Willen, kontinuierlich besser zu werden.

Eine Rolle, die das ganze Unternehmen verbindet.
Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Vertrieb, Customer Success, Technologie und Operations und hilfst dabei, aus Ideen Lösungen zu machen, die Kunden schätzen.

Verantwortung und Raum für Initiative.
Gute Ideen finden bei uns schnell Gehör. Du übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, Dinge voranzubringen, kannst auf die Unterstützung des Teams zählen und gestaltest mit, wie wir arbeiten.

Die Möglichkeit, mit Urban Connect zu wachsen.
Mit deinen Ergebnissen und Fähigkeiten wächst auch dein Verantwortungsbereich. Du hast die Chance, die nächste Entwicklungsphase unseres Unternehmens mitzugestalten.

Dazu kommen:

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und ein schönes Büro in Zürich.

  • Ein monatliches Mobilitätsbudget sowie Zugang zu unseren E-Bikes und geteilten E-Autos.

  • Ein motiviertes Team, das gerne gemeinsam und überwiegend vor Ort arbeitet, Wissen teilt und Erfolge zusammen feiert.

Bereit, etwas zu bewegen?

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar persönliche Zeilen: Warum Urban Connect? Was begeistert dich an der Zukunft der Mobilität? Und was hast du selbst in die Hand genommen und verbessert?

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

title: Intern Power Electronics Engineer
description:
With over 140 years of Swiss engineering heritage, Sécheron Hasler Group is a global leader in high-power electrical and electronic equipment. Our solutions power railways, renewable energy, DC and AC networks, and industrial systems worldwide trusted for their precision, reliability, and innovation.
At the heart of modern rail infrastructure, our Traction Power Systems unit delivers cutting-edge DC and AC traction substations, protection systems, power conversion and digital monitoring solutions. Join us to shape the future of sustainable mobility with technology that keeps cities and countries moving.

As an intern within our Traction Power Systems R&D team, you will support the development and validation of power electronic converters and control solutions used in railway and industrial applications. You will work alongside experienced engineers on innovative projects involving power conversion, control algorithms, testing, and system analysis.

The internship has the duration of 6 months and is expected to start in January 2027, but if that is not the best for you, let us know your availability.

Key responsibilities

  • Support the design and analysis of power electronic converters.
  • Assist in the development and validation of control algorithms.
  • Participate in laboratory testing, measurements, and troubleshooting activities.
  • Analyze simulation and test results and prepare technical reports.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement and innovation projects within the team.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams.

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Power Electronics, or a related field.
  • Strong interest in power converters, control systems, and electrical energy conversion.
  • Basic knowledge of power electronics and control theory.
  • Familiarity with simulation tools such as MATLAB/Simulink or similar is an advantage.
  • Curious, autonomous, and eager to learn in a hands-on engineering environment.
  • Good communication skills in English.

Benefits

A challenging internship in an international engineering environment.

Exposure to real-world power electronics and railway technology projects.

Mentorship from experienced R&D engineers.

Opportunity to develop practical skills in power conversion and control systems.
